selection_rationale: c1 best matches the programme goal (operational safety of LLM-generated NetOps changes), is experimentally falsifiable with a paired design, scored “pass” in critic review, and is feasible with available tooling (Batfish + hosted-model APIs). It directly tests a practical mitigation pattern (generate–validate–repair) under adversarial prompt injection and produces measurable, paired outcomes suited to CNSM’s Agentic AI Researcher track. Cited records: doi:10.36227/techrxiv.177004277.71795055/v1, https://openalex.org/W4388886073, https://openalex.org/W4403635865, https://openalex.org/W4389984066, https://openalex.org/W4389518608, https://openalex.org/W4391158659.
unresolved_uncertainties: Batfish (validator) coverage and false-negative rate relative to targeted vendor/configuration space.
Representativeness and diversity of the adversarial prompt-injection corpus for real-world attacks.
Sensitivity of the repair-loop outcome to prompt engineering and potential hosted-model API drift/hidden model-versioning.
External validity: sandbox/simulator results vs multi-vendor production topologies and real operational telemetry.
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Preregister and publish a Batfish coverage matrix and known gaps; include a plan to estimate validator false-negative rate (oracle/human spot-check sample).
Define and preregister the adversarial prompt-generation/red-team methodology, diversity metrics, and seed list to ensure reproducibility and breadth.
Preregister exact hosted-model identifiers/versions, full prompt templates, retry policy, model-call budget, and logging of provider metadata (timestamps, model-id in responses).
Include a sensitivity analysis plan across topology complexity and explicit multi-vendor synthetic variants; preregister inclusion/exclusion rules for topologies and tasks.
